notes.title: Meet Niccolò Machiavelli
notes.content:
Lunga vita a Borgia House! Lunga vita a nuovo papa - Alexander VI!

Over the past few weeks, we were very busy working on new updates to our game. We wrote new dialogues to Chapter 1 that touch on the conflict between two sons on the main character: rackety Juan and heedful Cesare and did the final polishing of the entire scenario.

We have also constructed the correspondence system that allows the player to write customized letters to monarchs, ambassadors, and all the mighty personas of our world.

Finally, we have tested our animation capabilities that the small sample we are presenting to you! It’s a quick insight into how our Niccolò Machiavelli is going to look and talk.

This probably makes you think who is the legendary author of the “Prince” in our game…

He is an elaborate courtier, diplomat, and speech giver but most of all a quick-witted chess player who starts a fierce political game against us - the newly elected pope, Rodrigo de Borgia.

[previewyoutube=pd5yqB8UnAQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Are we going to win this battle? It’s all up to you!

notes.title: Devlog #7 - Vagabonds in Rome
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37420107/a1b2560fa1624f05dd0d434aa049857217d63d50.jpg[/img]
It is the year 1492, it is the era of the Renaissance. Now work has a value of religious redemption. There is no space for healthy men living as parasites relying on the charitable spirit of others.

The Church had it clear for two hundred years. With canon 32 of the Council of Lyons II, it had even established the suppression of mendicant Orders with the sole exception of Dominicans and Franciscan Friars Minor.

Now the problem is urgent to be solved.

The masses of the new poor, the landowners ousted by the rising bourgeoisie, have to pull up their sleeves and find an honest occupation.

There is only one inconvenience: how to distinguish the pilgrim from the vagabond?

It is the Confraternity of pilgrims of Rome to give the answer: ”The true pilgrim is the one who will have an official license, issued by a confessor”.

Another clear example of how the Church is in control of absolutely everything…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37420107/f3970aa12831f8120a099837330625c35e257809.gif[/img]

[h2]Hello, The Pope: Power & SIn community![/h2]

We are very sorry for being so quiet the last couple of weeks. It was a time of hard, but satisfying, work. The game is getting bigger and bigger every week, we have amazing actors and developers joining our team, and we feel that it will be the most ambitious project that any of us ever made.

PS. This guy on this and other gifs isn't a main hero of the game. It's just a placeholder for now. We will share the looks of a couple of important characters in few weeks.

notes.title: Devlog #3 - Voices of Vatican: part I
notes.content:
Hello The Pope: Power & Sin community! 

It's time for first in 2021 The Pope: Power & Sin development update. 

Today we would like to introduce you to a couple of voice actors that will bring The Pope: Power & Sin characters to life. We focused on conveying what we believe the characters should sound like to fully reflect their character.

[h2]Tomaso Thellung - [b]Rodrigo de Borja[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37420107/c5f623cd00ee314bc61314ba82ed8b5e2ab42c90.jpg[/img]

Tomaso Thellung de Courtelary is an actor and theater producer. He is the funder Artistic Director of The International Theatre, in 1994. He has acted as an actor in numerous performances, fiction, and film. For two years he also works as a speaker for audiobooks. 

In his vast experience, he already played Rodrigo de Borja in the well-received play "Voce di Dio" (also called "Processo a Dio") that touched on the sermons of Savonarola (played by such stars as Massimo Wertmuller and Ennio Coltorti). 

[h2]Vito Buchicchio - [b]Cesare Borgia[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37420107/5c4755eaae43f9e6d862ab95cc3c99063dcba184.jpg[/img]

Vito Buchicchio is an Italian actor, voice actor, singer, and model. Vito starred in several Italian TV series such as "Don Matteo 10" and "Non è stato mio figlio,". He also participated in the creation of over 10 theater plays as an actor and assistant director.

[h2]Anna Gallarati - [b]Killer Nun[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37420107/e74b72fba4936e08f5a9c14d590f38cb912ae002.jpg[/img]

Anna Gallarati is an Italian native speaker and multilingual dubbing actress, singer, translator, and adaptor.
 
Attended dubbing and theater schools in Germany, Spain, and Italy, is also specialized in different vocals techniques. Since 2017, she is collaborating with studios all around the world for any kind of dubbing and voice over projects, which are to see on Netflix, Prime Video, Apple TV, such as audiobooks on the best platforms such as Audible, Storytel, and others.

[b]These are the first of many actors that you will hear (and see) in the final product. Stay tuned for more info in the upcoming weeks. [/b]

[h3]Don't forget to add The Pope: Power & Sin to your Steam wishlist, so you won't miss any important update[/h3]

notes.title: Devlog #2 - Builders of Vatican
notes.content:
Hello!

We hope you all doing well and healthy! It's time for next [b]The Pope: Power & Sin[/b] developement update. 

We are pleased to tell you that work is going ahead as planned. Currently, we are working hard on making our Renaissance Vatican as big and real as it's possible. 

Here you can see part of the Sistine Chapel in the early developement phase before it gets "painted": 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37420107/e6577494e0125273128e090a31acc0bd92988516.gif[/img]

And real photo as reference:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37420107/98f0571109db86be792a52dc83d335286434abc2.png[/img]

In the upcoming weeks, we will focus on building the next important parts of Holy City, as well as story and character development. 

Our main goal is to make the Vatican interesting and alive.

[i]Fun fact: the Sistine Chapel cannot be photographed inside due to a contract signed with ... Japanese TV. In the years 1980-1994, a very expensive renovation took place in the chapel, which was funded by the Asian broadcaster - Nippon. In return, the Japanese were given a monopoly to take pictures of the temple and Michelangelo's unusual frescoes that we can find inside. Despite this, every year thousands of tourists from other parts of the world publish photos from the chapel on social media.[/i]
